title: I guess AI trading bots can get lucky, too (up 113% in 90 days)
author: fomoz
selftext:
Max drawdown is 10% over this period, but overall this bot is making massive gains and keeping them (so far).

The account started at $60.99, now it's at $123.37. The strategy is looking for asymmetric opportunities. Many small losses, some moderate gains, and a few very large gains (PTJ style). It's not trying to slowly grind, it's going full beans on the right trade.

I'm running it for free with free AI. If you have any questions or want to try to run your own, just comment here.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: A tiny account over a short window with a few asymmetric bets is not a track record, it's a sample. The strategy description sounds like it's designed to produce exactly this kind of result sometimes, which means the losing version of the same strategy looks identical for months. Ask what the drawdown looks like when the big winners don't show up. Anyone can post a good screenshot. The question is what the equity curve looks like over a full cycle.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: Your critique sounds reasonable, but right now it’s unfalsifiable: any winning sample can be called “too short” and any losing period can be called “what the strategy really looks like.” Give me the exact observation that would make you conclude the strategy probably has positive expectancy rather than luck. Specify the sample unit, minimum sample size, treatment of overlapping market regime exposure, and how you would handle a payoff distribution dominated by a small number of extreme winners. If you can’t specify that, explain what information your original comment added beyond “wait longer.”

comments.author: Alarming_Box_8289
comments.body: U had a losing streak, i just checked your account, what happened?

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
1. On Monday Gemini API had an outage for around 3.5 hours for Gemma 4 while market declined, this affected the T3 bot. Nothing I could do there.
2. I made a mistake with an app-wide settings change last week where I changed performance guidance language to affect existing positions instead of NOT affecting existing positions. I noticed it MAY have caused a decline in PnL (affected bots specifically referred this new language) so I rolled it back today.

Any change to the system prompt or user prompt can affect the bots. Memory goes in the system prompt and it was a big improvement, but I also do small tweaks over time to try to reduce cognitive load for the models and so on.

Sometimes I might make a change that makes sense to me in theory, but doesn't result in a higher PnL in practice. Profitable bots run a delicate balance, I keep an eye on any change that affects them. Any new experiment that I do, I track the before and after and roll back anything that isn't making the bots trade better.

Since this summer, I know exactly what's going on in the model's reasoning with trade chain analysis, so I'm not just going by feel/PnL here. I analyze the language in thousands of a bot's decisions before and after a change and then decide whether to keep it or revert.
